# Testament of Reuben — 1
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

These are Reuben's dying words to his sons — a confession no father would want to give, but this one couldn't leave without giving it.

**1** He was 125 years old when he called them together. **2** He told them straight: I'm dying. I'm going where our fathers went. **3** Judah was there, and Gad, and Levi — all his brothers. **4** He said: Listen to me, brothers. Hear what Reuben your brother has to tell you. **5** I call the God of heaven as my witness: do not walk in the sins of your youth, do not give yourself to sexual sin the way I did — the sin that defiled my father Jacob's bed. **6** For that sin, God struck my loins with a terrible plague — seven months of agony. **7** Only my father Jacob's prayers kept me alive. **8** I was thirty years old. Seven months I was sick. **9** For seven years after that I drank no wine, ate no meat, tasted nothing pleasant. I mourned my sin. And it was a great sin — nothing like it had been done in Israel. **10** My father never stopped praying for me — because I had sinned against Bilhah, the one he loved.

Now hear what I saw in those years of repentance. I saw the seven spirits that war against a man.

**11** Seven spirits are stationed against every human being, set by Beliar, lords over the sins of youth: **12** The first is the spirit of sexual sin — it lives in the body's desires. **13** The second is insatiability — it lives in the gut. **14** The third is the spirit of fighting — it lives in the liver. **15** The fourth is flattery and manipulation — making yourself look beautiful so others will be used. **16** The fifth is pride — arrogance that puffs up. **17** The sixth is lying — it works through jealousy and spite, hiding the truth from family and friends. **18** The seventh is injustice — it steals, it schemes, it says the heart's desire justifies every means.

**19** These seven are why even the Watchers fell — they looked at the daughters of men and could not stop looking. **20** And fornication is the mother of them all. It separates a person from God and drags them toward Beliar.

**21** So don't stare at a woman's face. Don't be alone with another man's wife. Stay away from entanglements with women. **22** If I hadn't seen Bilhah bathing, I wouldn't have fallen into this catastrophe. **23** My mind held onto what I'd seen and wouldn't let me sleep until I'd done the thing. **24** Jacob my father was away. Bilhah was drunk, asleep, uncovered in her room. **25** I went in. I saw her. I did what I did. I left before she woke up. And immediately, an angel told my father everything.

**26** Sons, do not let a woman's beauty lead you off a cliff. Kings have fallen this way. Kingdoms have fallen. **27** Samson — brought down by a woman. Solomon — seduced, destroyed. **28** But Joseph kept himself pure, and became a blessing to all the world. **29** Women weaponize beauty because they lack other power over men. What they can't win openly, they take by craft.

**30** The angel told me this: women are more susceptible to the spirit of fornication than men are — and they plot against men in their hearts. **31** First they capture the eye. Then through the eye they pour poison into the mind. Then, once the act is done, they hold the captive.

**32** So flee from sexual sin, my sons. Tell your wives and daughters not to dress to deceive — for every woman who uses that kind of power has reserved for herself a bitter judgment. **33** That's how the Watchers were brought down — they kept looking and couldn't stop, and the women sensed their hunger and leaned into it. **34** Guard your senses. Bid the women around you to guard theirs. Because even when nothing happens, the constant proximity is a disease that doesn't heal.

**35** There is no wisdom in fornication, no reverence for God. Just jealousy, and distance from God, and destruction.

**36** So here is my final word, my sons: do not stare at beauty. Walk with a simple heart in the fear of God. Work hard. Tend your flocks. Wait for the wife God gives you. **37** I couldn't look my father in the face until he died. The shame still lives in me. But his prayers covered me, and the LORD's anger passed. **38** From then on I did not sin again. You can do the same. **39** Keep what I have told you, and you will not fall into the pit that I fell into — the pit of fornication, which separates the soul from God and drags it down to Hades before its time.

---
*End of Testament of Reuben*
